runs.text:
When did Google make Kotlin its preferred language for Android?
Vote 👇 

Careful, there’s an earlier date that trips people up.

Google added first-class Kotlin support back in 2017, and then went fully Kotlin-first at Google I/O 2019, declaring it the preferred language for Android development. Since then, new Android APIs and guidance are designed Kotlin-first. In 2024, Google also announced official support for Kotlin Multiplatform

Kotlin is turning 15, but when did it really begin?
The very first commit was pushed before the public reveal. Can you guess the year?

Kotlin’s first commit landed on November 8, 2010, roughly eight months before JetBrains unveiled the language in July 2011. That’s why 2026 marks Kotlin turning 15, the perfect reason to celebrate how far a quietly started JVM project has come.
